language_instruction: **Source language:** Classical (literary) Mongolian in the traditional Uighur-Mongol vertical script, printed from woodblocks (Beijing Kanjur, 1718–20). It is NOT Manchu. Columns run top to bottom and are read from LEFT to RIGHT. Transcribe in Mongolian script (Unicode U+1800 block), one source column per line, in reading order. The margin carries a Chinese section/volume/folio label. Report the primary language in the <language> tag.

translation.text:
<meta>Page number: nigen qoyar / 二 (First volume, folio two)</meta>
<note>Red woodblock-printed double-line rectangular frame with a floral scrollwork border enclosing the text panel and marginal cartouches.</note>
<margin>First volume, folio two <note>original: "ᠨᠢᠭᠡ ᠳ᠋ᠦᠭᠡᠷ ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠨ ᠬᠤᠶᠠᠷ"</note></margin>
Of <term>Vajrapani</term> <gloss>the Thunderbolt-Holder, a protective bodhisattva embodying the power of all Buddhas</gloss>, the assembly,
through devotion to you,
deeply bows and confesses in reverence.
O <term>Vajrapani</term> <gloss>Thunderbolt-Holder</gloss>, your
melodious voice and decree
are like the light of the sun:
our minds,
illuminate them! The decree of the <term>Bhagavan</term> <gloss>the Victoriously Passed Beyond, an epithet of the Buddha; Mongolian: ilaju tegüs nögčigsen</gloss>:
endowed with peerless, great
compassion in full perfection,
the manifestly awakening teacher,
the decree of the <term>Bhagavan</term> <gloss>Blessed One</gloss>,
is a single great sunlight:
dispel the darkness of <term>klesha</term> <gloss>mental afflictions and defilements; Mongolian: nisvanis</gloss>,
and in those directions,
throughout the <term>trichiliocosm</term> <gloss>the three-thousandfold great thousand world system of Buddhist cosmology; Mongolian: gurban minggan yirtinčü</gloss>,
may the <term>mandala</term> <gloss>sacred cosmogram or sphere of awakening</gloss> flourish; without the entire assembly
even knowing, grant me bliss!
Through the devotion of the assembly,
we deeply bow and confess in reverence;
O leader of the companions of the assembly,
<margin>Scripture of Various Chapters, Scroll Seven, Part One, Folio Two <note>original: "諸品經第七卷上 二"</note></margin>

<summary>A devotional Buddhist hymn in Mongolian addressed to the bodhisattva Vajrapani, praising his enlightening speech and the compassionate decree of the Bhagavan as a great sun that dispels the darkness of mental afflictions across the three-thousandfold universe.</summary>
